channel.title: 3mpwr App - Curated Disability News
channel.description: Daily curated news on disability rights, accessibility, and benefits across Canada

item.title: Fire at federal government building in Toronto probed as suspected arson
item.description: Toronto emergency services say a fire has been extinguished after it started in a federal government building in the city. Police said a man is in custody.

item.title: Duty free shops say they're still losing sales as Canada-U.S. cross-border travel plummets
item.description: Owners of duty free shops in Windsor and Sarnia say they continue to suffer the fall-out from the U.S. trade war, seeing drops in business in the 30 per cent range year over year.

item.title: Alberta’s Health-Care Privatization Push Is Heading to Disaster
item.description: The UCP government has chosen a discredited ideology over real solutions.

item.title: Couple from Gatineau, Que., found dead while vacationing in Dominican Republic
item.description: The son of Alain Noël and Christine Sauvé found their bodies inside the couple's vacation home on Boxing Day, the family told Radio-Canada.
item.dc:creator: 3mpwr App Curator

item.title: Pimicikamak Cree Nation declares state of emergency after power outage in northern Manitoba
item.description: Residents of a northern Manitoba First Nation are being told that their power will not be restored until late in the day on New Year’s Eve. Pimicikamak Cree Nation declared a state of emergency on Monday following a widespread power outage in the Cross Lake area around 11:30 p.m. Sunday.

item.title: 'Frustration at its pinnacle:' Ontario newcomers anxious over immigration overhaul
item.description: Concerned about recent changes to immigration in Ontario, Muhammad Haseeb Ahmad is anxiously awaiting word on whether he can become a Canadian permanent resident.

item.title: Saskatoon police to start mandatory alcohol screenings in new year on traffic stops
item.description: Other police forces in Canada have implemented mandatory alcohol screening since the Criminal Code was amended in 2018 to allow for breathalyzers without cause in traffic stops.

item.title: Northeast B.C. measles outbreak to continue into 2026, health officials say
item.description: Six months after a measles outbreak first began in northeast B.C., Northern Health says the virus will continue to circulate in the region well into 2026, prolonging the strain on healthcare workers and keeping vulnerable people at risk.

item.title: Vancouver Whitecaps reach proposed settlement in lawsuit seeking damages for 2024 Messi no-show
item.description: Fan alleged "bait-and-switch" in lawsuit launched after international superstars Lionel Messi, Luis Suarez and Sergio Busquet didn't show up as advertised with Inter Miami to play the Vancouver Whitecaps.

item.title: RCMP union cuts into Alberta Next Panel for ‘politically driven' recommendation to shed Mounties
item.description: The RCMP union says the Alberta Next panel is trying to revive an idea already been rejected by Albertans, using outdated references and inaccurate policy to justify its stance.

item.title: Ministry urges Saskatchewan drivers to be safe on the road around snowplows
item.description: Ministry of Highways says in 2019, they saw four collisions, jumping up to 12 in 2024, and that when driving around snowplows you should be alert, slow down, and give space.
